### Watch screen
- Dialogs a page opens (alert, confirm, prompt, leave-page) are drawn on its tile the way Chrome shows them. A print preview gets its own tile with the real preview, and Chrome permission requests ("access other devices on your local network", location, notifications…) get their own tile drawn like Chrome's bubble, in the slot color. Shown only; you answer them in the browser window.
- Permission requests are read on Windows from the window title and on macOS through Accessibility (only that slot's Chrome, by process ID; nothing is shown without the Accessibility permission). Popup windows appear as tiles.
- Fixed tab connections piling up when the watch page was hidden and shown again (10 hide/show cycles: 5 → 14 connections; now stays at 5).
- Background tabs whose title keeps changing (unread counters, clocks) are captured at most once per 30 s, so they aren't kept rendering.
- Tabs opened in the background (e.g. moved from another slot) no longer stay frozen half-loaded: after a change they are captured again at 3, 10 and 30 s.
- Dashed drop preview when dragging a tile, × to close a tab on its tile; a re-render during a drag can no longer move the wrong tab.
- The server stays up while any slot runs; it doesn't scan when nobody is watching and scans every 5 s while every watch page is hidden. Hidden pages and folded slots get no frames.
- The page can't be framed by other sites (clickjacking), slot numbers outside 1–99 are refused, and "Close slot" force-ends only the PID the browser reports (not a possibly reused PID from the registry).
- Pause/resume notices show as "Slot 3 paused" in the message panel. `cdpm watch --cols 4` no longer reads the 4 as a slot number.

### Page actions
- A button below the fold covered by a popup is no longer clicked: the cover check passed viewport coordinates where document coordinates were expected and was silently skipped on scrolled pages.
- Elements inside cross-site iframes: the frame offset is re-measured after scrolling, and a popup on the outer page covering the iframe blocks the click.
- `network_idle` waits no longer always time out on pages with cross-site iframes (the iframe document request stayed "in flight" forever; test page 20 s → 1.4 s).
- No more 30 s "still loading" after SPA back buttons (`history.back`), cancelled navigations, or a leave-page dialog.
- Punctuation is typed with real US-layout key codes, and capitals/shifted symbols press and release Shift.
- Waiting for a removed element to become enabled fails at once with "take a new snapshot" instead of waiting up to 10 minutes. A crashed tab's connection is dropped and re-attached.

### Signals and blocking
- Fixed vendor blocking turning off after visiting the vendor's own site, and notices naming vendors seen on a previous site.
- Same-site app endpoints (`/api/events`…) are no longer counted as telemetry; two common Cloudflare cookies and 403s from iframes no longer trigger notices.
- The shared-worker guard no longer attaches repeatedly; block patterns are compiled once; quiet-blocked fetch/XHR get `{}`.

### Launching, registry, tools
- CDPM no longer restarts a browser it didn't launch (Edge/Brave started by hand on a slot port) as plain Chrome after mistaking it for an outdated Chrome — a proxied slot could have come back without its proxy. A failed update-restart leaves the open URLs in a slot message.
- Fixed races: deleting a record another session just rewrote, two processes taking the auto-setup lock; locks no longer stay forever when Windows reuses a PID.
- CLAUDE.md with unbalanced CDPM markers is left alone with a message. `--browser Chrome` (any case) uses the normal profile. A port grabbed by another program during launch is reported right away. Icon files are written atomically and an icon failure no longer fails a launch.
- `interactive` + `ref` snapshots keep the region; `browser_download_wait` delivers the message that stopped it; shorter results (no single-page footer, only changed tabs in the header); CDPM's own notes sit outside the page-content fence.
- Tests: 86 unit, 64 integration, run on macOS and Windows. Memory stayed flat in a 3,000-round long run, 3 sessions × 600 rounds, and 1,200 rounds of watch/signals/blocking churn.
